processed_notes.note_text:
Focus: Education, Employment, Accountability, Relationships, and Transition Planning

During this week’s case management meeting, Christian discussed the importance of responding appropriately to criticism and being responsible with his free time. He demonstrated increased awareness of how his choices and responses can affect his progress and opportunities.

Christian identified obtaining his GED as an important educational goal. He stated that his goal for the upcoming week is to enroll in adult education so he can continue his education, eventually attend college, and pursue a certification that will benefit his future employment and independence.

Christian also discussed the importance of taking his transition into the community one step at a time. He acknowledged that having too much freedom or access to movement too quickly could potentially expose him to situations that may trigger old habits. He expressed a desire to remain mindful of his environment, recognize potential triggers, and avoid moving faster than he feels prepared to manage responsibly.

Christian reflected on his relationship with his mother and recognized the importance of taking gradual steps to rebuild trust and demonstrate responsibility. He understands that his mother is aware of the risks associated with his transition back into society and stated that he wants to show through his actions that he can handle increased responsibility appropriately.

Regarding employment, Christian acknowledged that obtaining major employment may be difficult at this time due to an injury. He is therefore considering entry-level restaurant employment, such as working as a dishwasher or cook, as a practical way to meet his current responsibilities while continuing to work toward his larger educational and career goals.

Christian also discussed managing his social media use. He reported that people continue to reach out to him through social media and recognized that excessive communication and online activity can become a distraction from his goals. He stated that he is working on limiting his social media use and maintaining focus on his priorities.

Christian demonstrated increased insight into the importance of maintaining realistic expectations for himself and for the people providing support in his life. He recognized that unrealistic expectations, if not managed appropriately, can lead to disappointment, conflict, or missed opportunities. Christian appears to be developing a more realistic understanding of his current circumstances and the importance of progressing through his goals one step at a time.

Plan/Action Steps:

1. Enroll in an adult education/GED program during the upcoming week.
2. Explore realistic entry-level employment opportunities that accommodate his current injury.
3. Continue practicing appropriate responses to criticism and feedback.
4. Limit social media use to reduce distractions and unwanted influences.
5. Identify potential triggers and practice making decisions that support his transition goals.
6. Continue building trust with his mother and support system through consistent responsible actions.
7. Continue setting realistic expectations and focusing on manageable short-term goals.

Progress Summary:
Christian demonstrated increased self-awareness, accountability, and willingness to make gradual changes. He identified education, employment, healthy relationships, responsible use of free time, and managing outside influences as important areas of focus. He appears motivated to take practical steps toward independence while recognizing the importance of patience, structure, and maintaining a support system.

Strengths:
Christian shared that he is proud of the progress he has made. He was surprised to hear that his family, especially his mother, is proud of him. He believes his family sees that he is making better decisions and is more willing to support him.

Discussion/Intervention:
Christian discussed how blaming others contributed to problems in his past, including substance use and poor decisions. He stated that he is proud of himself for consistently attending his required groups instead of returning to old behaviors.

Christian also shared that CBT has helped him see the value of his education. He stated that he once felt his education was worthless, but now understands that what he learned can help him understand his behavior and make better decisions. He especially connected with the difference between reacting and responding and wants to practice thinking before making decisions.

Christian reported that he has been looking for employment that will work with his upcoming surgery. His immediate goal is to schedule his surgery, continue attending classes, find employment, obtain his own housing, and maintain his sobriety.

Christian also discussed old friends trying to contact him through fake social media pages. He stated that he does not want to return to the person he used to be and wants to continue becoming a better version of himself.

Skill Practiced:
Christian identified responsibility as the skill he wants to practice. He understands that rebuilding trust with his family will take time and that his actions will show his progress.

Next Steps:

* Schedule his medical appointment/surgery.
* Continue attending CBT and required groups.
* Continue maintaining sobriety.
* Continue looking for employment.
* Practice responding instead of reacting.
* Maintain healthy boundaries with people from his past.
* Continue working toward independent housing and stability.

Intake Case Meeting Note:
Christian is a 30-year-old Spartanburg native who recently returned to the community on August 10 after serving approximately 8 months in county for Burglary 3rd. He is currently on 3 years of probation and resides at Oxford House. He has reliable transportation and recently obtained his ID. Christian did not complete high school and reports a history of homelessness and street involvement. He also has a history of methamphetamine use and is currently participating in rehabilitation.

Christian passed his drug screen and appears to be a great fit for the Turn 90 program. He expressed motivation to make positive changes, build self-value, and establish stability.

Goals: Pay approximately $3,000 in fees needed to reinstate his driver’s license, obtain job training and work experience, earn OSHA and other certifications, and possibly attend school to pursue a CDL. He also wants to maintain sobriety by surrounding himself with positive, recovery-minded people, secure his own housing, and develop a healthy and productive daily lifestyle and environment
